claims.text: In situ HRTEM with an integrated heating stage will reveal atomic-scale structural changes in nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at high temperature.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a homogeneous, well-mixed alloy structure at room temperature.
A specialized in-chamber HRTEM heating stage can apply controlled high-temperature heating to the nanoparticles.
The nanoparticles can be monitored in real time at high temperature in vacuum or inert gas.
Atomic-scale lattice distortions can be observed by HRTEM during heating.
Defect nucleation can be observed by HRTEM during heating.
Incipient phase separation can be observed by HRTEM during heating.
Thermodynamic contributions at elevated temperature trigger subtle atomic rearrangements in the nanoparticles.
Elevated-temperature thermodynamic effects can produce phase transitions in the nanoparticles.
Thermally induced atomic rearrangements and phase transitions lead to observable changes in lattice structure.
Heating will produce lattice-parameter shifts, defect formation, or phase-separation events that are absent at room temperature.
Room-temperature HRTEM images will show uniform atomic ordering with minimal defects or phase heterogeneity.
Spatial resolution and heating uniformity can limit detection of thermally induced structural changes.
Electron-beam damage can generate structural changes that may be mistaken for thermal effects.
Atomic-resolution HRTEM images can be used to measure lattice spacing, defect density, and phase-boundary evolution.
